Connect to foundations: The virial theorem: why shrinking stars heat up ↗ Compare solution assumptions and boundary data in the solution library ↗ 01The same equations can select different flows Begin with continuity, momentum and mass for a spherical self-gravitating isothermal gas. Cooling maintaining isothermality is supplied; rotation and fields are omitted. The sign of time relative to central formation and the outer density/velocity select the solution. 02Introduce post-formation similarity variables Set central formation at t = 0 and use t > 0 here. Match time powers in each term to reduce partial differential equations to ordinary equations in x. x=rcst, u=csv(x), ρ=α(x)4πGt², M=cs³tGm(x) m=x²α(x−v), m′=x²α [(x−v)²−1]v′=[α(x−v)−2x](x−v) [(x−v)²−1]α′α=[α−2(x−v)x](x−v) A regular sonic point x−v = 1 also requires α = 2/x. Directly dividing by the vanishing denominator fails; select a regular critical branch together with global boundary conditions. 03Shu: inside-out collapse from a singular isothermal sphere x≥1 : v=0, α=2x², ρ=cs²2πGr² x→0 : m→m₀, v≈−√(2m₀x), α≈√(m₀2x³) The exterior is a static singular isothermal sphere, with an expansion wave at x = 1 marking the onset of infall. Inner r⁻³ᐟ² density and free-fall velocity apply where central mass dominates. Use the supplied global-solution result m₀ ≈ 0.975. Ṁ=m₀cs³G, Mcentral=m₀cs³tG 04LPH: an envelope already flowing inward The Larson–Penston flow continued through central formation by Hunter has α ≈ 8.86/x² and v ≈ −3.28 far away. The envelope is about 4.43 times denser than Shu’s static sphere and is already infalling. Its central coefficient is m₀ ≈ 46.9. The panel numerically computes the post-formation Shu and LPH similarity ODEs. Compare log–log density and inward-speed profiles, switch to similarity coordinates, and animate labelled mass shells. The approximate LPH central accretion coefficient 46.9 differs from the pre-formation LP flux and is not a universal finite-cloud rate. 05Separate the derived equations from supplied eigenvalues The similarity equations and free-fall powers can be followed here. Coefficients 0.975 and 46.9 depend on boundary conditions and critical branches, not dimensions alone. The plots integrate the intermediate region from Shu’s A → 2⁺ limit and the LPH outer data, measuring the inner m₀. Checks use Shu (1977), Table 2, free-fall limits, mass conservation and half-step convergence. Rounded LPH outer coefficients give m₀ ≈ 46.97. Finite reservoirs, disks, fields and heating change real accretion. Compare with collapse from a finite initial equilibrium such as a Bonnor–Ebert sphere, and inspect what was imposed at infinity. Compare high-density molecular conversion with a gravitational clock in three-body chemistry. CHECK YOUR UNDERSTANDING Pause and work it out. Within one solution family, double sound speed and compare at the same time after central formation. How do rate, central mass and similarity radius scale? Show the answer and reasoning The rate and central mass increase by eight; cₛt doubles. The coefficient m₀ depends on the solution family. Changing sound speed alone does not switch between Shu and LPH. REFERENCES & PHYSICAL INPUTS Explanations and derivations are written for this guide. References may use different notation or normalization. Panel methods and approximations are stated in the text.
